# ShipGuard CLI
> The deterministic, local security and config check that runs inside your agent loop: same diff, same verdict, a real exit code your agent can read. One command checks a project for leaked secrets, unprotected routes, destructive database migrations, unverified payment webhooks and risky deploy settings. It runs locally, gives the same answer every time, and your code never leaves your machine.

ShipGuard is not a code reviewer and not a general security scanner. It uses plain pattern rules (no AI model). It informs: the verdict is in the JSON `recommendation` field (SAFE_TO_SHIP, REVIEW_BEFORE_SHIP, DO_NOT_SHIP). The exit code is 0 whenever the scan completes; add --strict to make it exit 1 on a blocking result.

## Install
npx @agenticcli/shipguard scan
npm install -g @agenticcli/shipguard

## Commands
shipguard init — initialize policy file
shipguard scan — scan project for risks
shipguard scan --changed — scan only changed files (not for CI: a clean checkout has nothing to compare)
shipguard scan --strict — exit code 1 on a blocking result or an unfinished scan (opt-in hard gate, free on every plan)
shipguard scan --report — generate Markdown report
shipguard scan --json — machine-readable output (schemaVersion 6; the `coverage` object says how many files were discovered, scanned and skipped, and why)
shipguard scan --check-regressions — exit code 1 if a previously-passing rule now fails
shipguard hook — install the gate as a git hook (--target claude or --target ci for Claude Code or GitHub Actions)
shipguard history — show recent local scan history for this repo (read-only)
shipguard schema --json — the machine-readable contract: verdicts, exit codes, limits

## Risk Categories
- Secrets: hardcoded API keys, committed .env files, frontend exposure
- Auth: unprotected admin routes, missing auth middleware
- Payments: Stripe/Razorpay webhook signature verification
- Database: destructive SQL migrations, schema risks
- Deployment: CORS misconfiguration, debug mode, missing headers

## Target Users
Solo SaaS builders, indie hackers, small dev teams using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Lovable
